Portal v0.5 This week Activities Calendar Policies FAQ Quick answers New families Glossary This week / Armonia / Drama Armonia · Drama Every child on stage. Drama at Armonia is part of one package: music, drama and dance performance, together. Children work with voice, character and movement, and along the way they grow in confidence and learn to carry a piece as a team. What a session feels like A rehearsal room, not a classroom. Sessions run in small groups, and the same group returns week after week, so a scene has time to grow. Children try a moment one way and then another: how a line sounds, how a character stands, how a movement lands. Getting it wrong in front of friends is part of the work, and that is where the confidence comes from. What a performance feels like The performances children work toward are ELC occasions, with the whole school behind them. At a drama night nobody auditions for a place: every child takes a part, and every child gets a moment at the centre of the stage. A Night in Sherwood filled the hall with families for an evening the children carried from start to finish. Read the story on our blog. The whole cast on stage at A Night in Sherwood In the The

Portal v0.5 This week Activities Calendar Policies FAQ Quick answers New families Glossary This week / Armonia / Expressive languages Armonia · Expressive languages Languages of thought. In expressive languages, children explore their ideas through drawing, painting and building, treating each material as another language for thinking. They work with real materials and real tools, and a piece can carry over many sessions until it says what they mean. What a session feels like A studio, not an art lesson. Children choose a material and get to work: clay, wire, paint, light, paper, found objects. The adult watches closely and asks the next question rather than showing the answer. Children work in small groups and return to their work week after week, so a drawing or a build has time to grow until it carries the meaning they intend. Armonia is ELC's enrichment programme for children in Years 4 to 6, bringing music, drama and dance performance together. Sessions run on Tuesday and Thursday afternoons from 3 to 4pm. Children work in small groups and return to their work week after week, so ideas have time to grow. Performances through the school year give children a real audience for what they rehearse and make. The week rhythm Tuesday and Thursday, 3pm to 4pm This is the current rhythm, for Years 4 to 6. Children stay on after the school day ends and work with the same small group each week. What Armonia feels like Performances anchor the Armonia year, and they belong to a school that loves putting children on stage. At ELC's drama nights nobody auditions for a place: every child takes a part, whether the evening is a full production like A Night in Sherwood or light and shadow work in the Theatre of the Imagination. Portal v0.5 This week Activities Calendar Policies FAQ Quick answers New families Glossary This week / Armonia / Music Armonia · Music Learning you can hear. Music at Armonia is part of one package: music, drama and dance performance, together. Making music feeds nearly every part of how a child grows: thinking, feeling, movement and language, and with them the quieter habits of self-discipline and confidence. What a session feels like Small groups, real instruments. Children play alone and together, from a single line to a full ensemble, and both matter: musicianship stretches how a young brain organises itself and grows. The same group returns week after week, so a piece has time to get good before anyone else hears it. What a performance feels like A concert is a child's way of showing their family what they have been learning, and at ELC the whole community turns up to listen. When the school stages a musical, whole year groups share the stage: Wonderland the Musical packed the courtyard at night, with every child making a role their own. Read the story on our blog. Portal v0.5 This week Activities Calendar Policies FAQ Quick answers New families Glossary This week / Armonia / Science Armonia · Science Real questions, tested. Science here is hands-on investigation. Children start from their own questions, test their thinking with real materials, and follow the evidence wherever it leads. What a session feels like A workshop, not a worksheet. Science sessions start from children's own questions, and children test their thinking with real materials and careful observation. They practise the habits scientists actually use: noticing closely, predicting, checking and trying again. That is how children already work across ELC. One Year 4 class designed a planet of its own, debating its size, core and terrain as a group, then put its questions directly to a NASA scientist, whose advice was to stay curious and keep asking. The same habits carry into the garden, where children watch what grows and work out why. Portal v0.5 This week Activities Calendar Policies FAQ Quick answers New families Glossary This week / Armonia / Technology Armonia · Technology Making, not just using. Technology here means making, code and robotics as tools for ideas. Children move from using technology to building with it, designing things that respond to what they imagine. What a session feels like Build, test, build again. In technology sessions children move from using technology to making with it, designing and building things that respond to their ideas. Children at ELC already work this way. A Year 3 class sketched robot designs in their notebooks, then worked together to code a real robot's movements, and children in the rewilding project designed and built machines that answered real needs they had noticed in the school garden. It rarely works the first time, and that is the point: children read what went wrong, change one thing and build again. Who can collect your child Authorisation lanyards Your child is released only to an adult carrying an ELC authorisation lanyard for your family. Portal v0.5 This week Activities Calendar Policies FAQ Quick answers New families Glossary This week / Community / Giving La Comunità · Giving From me to we. Giving at ELC starts with the children. In the sala, the school's gathering place, they build connections with each other, with their teachers and with the world, and somewhere in that the me becomes a we. The fundraising this community does grows out of exactly that. What this community has done Class artworks on their easels for the Art from the Heart raffle. For Art from the Heart, every class made a collaborative artwork and families bought raffle tickets to take one home. The money raised went to the Pediatric Cardiac Surgery Foundation to fund life-saving heart surgery. Read the story on our blog. Families making together at a charity book and bake day. Charity days here have a familiar shape: children and parents making, baking and selling together, and children learning along the way that privilege carries a duty to others. Read the story on our blog. The giving reaches beyond the school gates too. Families have been invited to stand with the Bookworm Foundation, which works for equal reading opportunities for children

Workshops, social mornings and other events that bring the ELC community together: children and parents. La Comunità is how we turn a school into a place families belong. What these occasions are like Social mornings are the easiest place to start: coffee, no agenda, and other families who walk the same route as you. Dates for each one are on the calendar. Parent workshops go one layer deeper, bringing a specialist to the questions parents actually carry. One workshop on positive parenting kept returning to a single idea: trust, in yourself as a parent and in your child. Read the story on our blog. Parents led the country pavilions at the Carnival of Cultures. The Carnival of Cultures celebrated the many cultures inside this one school community, and parents ran the country pavilions themselves. Read the story on our blog. Over the hurdles at Fun Field Day. And Fun Field Day brought the whole school onto the field for a day of games and team spirit, with older children helping younger ones through the course. h: Photographs, and the choice that stays yours.
b: Portal v0.5 This week Activities Calendar Policies FAQ Quick answers New families Glossary This week / Policies / Photo consent Photographs and consent Photographs, and the choice that stays yours. We photograph learning as it happens, and we publish only what your consent allows. If you ever want an image taken down, one email is all it takes. What we photograph, and why WHY Learning as it happens Teachers photograph children at work: building, painting, presenting, playing. These images document how learning unfolds, and they come back to you and your child as part of the record of the year. WHY Moments worth keeping Celebrations, performances and trips are photographed so families can share in them, on the calendar, in letters home and on school displays. How consent works HOW Your choices, from the enrolment pack When you joined, the enrolment pack asked how your child's image may be used: inside school only, in letters home, or on public school channels. Those choices are what we follow. HOW You can change your mind Consent is not fixed for the year. Tell the office your choice has changed and we update your child's record. h: What this site knows about you: nothing.
b: Portal v0.5 This week Activities Calendar Policies FAQ Quick answers New families Glossary This week / Privacy Privacy What this site knows about you: nothing. No login. No accounts. No cookies. No trackers. No child data. This page explains what that means, and where your information does live when you sign up for something. A promise you can check This site is a set of plain pages. It sets no cookies, keeps no accounts, loads no advertising scripts, and serves everything, including its fonts, from its own address. We count which pages get opened so we know what helps; the counter stores the page address and nothing else; there is no cookie, no fingerprint, and nothing that identifies you, and you can verify this in your browser's developer tools. If you install this site as an app, the pages are stored on your own device so they open offline. Only that page-open count is ever sent back to us. Where your information does go Some links on this site take you to the systems that run registration and feedback. h: Worried about a child? Say something.
b: Portal v0.5 This week Activities Calendar Policies FAQ Quick answers New families Glossary This week / Report a concern Safeguarding Worried about a child? Say something. You do not need to be sure, and you do not need proof. If something feels wrong, tell us and let the people trained for this take it from there. This page is here for the rare moment something feels wrong, but the care behind it runs all year. Every child's safety and wellbeing comes first at ELC, and that is a promise the whole community keeps together, with teachers and families in partnership. Read the story on our blog. Who to speak to Speak to any teacher or the school office, in person or by email: . They will bring in the campus safeguarding lead the same day. Named safeguarding leads for each campus are being added to this page. What happens after you report Your concern goes to the campus safeguarding lead, who decides the next step the same day. The school follows a written process, from first report to action: you can read the safeguarding triage chart and the full safeguarding and child protection policy. You will be taken seriously, and raising a concern in good faith is always the right thing to do.

What a try-out is, what it is not, and the season ahead: the dates, the four sports, and where sign-up happens. What a try-out is A try-out is a session Your child trains with the coaches, and the coaches see their level and where they fit. That is all it is: a normal session with people watching carefully. A try-out is not a place Squads are selected, so trying out does not guarantee a spot. Every child gets clear feedback either way, so you know where things stand and what comes next. The season, in order Where sign-up happens All sport sign-up starts on the Activities page. Go there, pick sport, and follow the registration link. h: How to know a message is really from ELC.
The official channels, all of them
b: Portal v0.5 This week Activities Calendar Policies FAQ Quick answers New families Glossary This week / Is it really us Verify How to know a message is really from ELC. Scammers target school parents in Bangkok, often over LINE, and often about money. Here is how to check any message in ten seconds. The official channels, all of them This site: portal.elc.ac.th The school website: elc.ac.th Email from an address ending @elc.ac.th, and nothing else The Parent App, for your child's learning Three rules that never change We never ask for payment through LINE chat or any other chat message. We never ask you to pay into a personal bank account. School payments go to the school. We never rush you. A real school message survives you taking a day to check it. When something feels off Stop. Pay nothing, click nothing, reply to nothing. Contact the school office yourself, using an address you already know, not one from the suspicious message: Checking a real message costs a minute. Trusting a fake one can cost a term's fees. We would always rather answer a "was this you?" email. portal.elc.ac.th · ELC International Schools, Thong Lor No login needed.
